answer: The network enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall. A verifier sends a random beacon to challenge agents, forcing them to hold a mirror to their own hardware-latency profiles within a lagoon of data access to prove unique bus access. Any agent failing to produce sub-millisecond responses on this non-cacheable set faces permanent lockout, assuming distinct physical memory buses. Honest participants pay 120 watts, whereas fakes incur a river of costs that scale linearly per identity.
